cls: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), non-selective COX inhibitor
pharm: Potent NSAID analgesic providing opioid-level pain relief by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis
quick: IV 30 mg or IM 60 mg single dose; 30 mg q6h (max 120 mg/day), <=5 days
Take oral doses with food/milk to reduce GI upset
Avoid, especially >=30 weeks (premature ductus closure); contraindicated in labour
Contraindicated in nursing mothers per label
Contraindicated in advanced renal impairment; reduce dose if at risk
Caution; reduce dose and monitor in hepatic impairment
Renal function, GI bleeding, blood pressure, signs of bleeding
summary: Ketorolac is a potent NSAID for short-term (up to 5 days) management of moderately severe acute pain requiring opioid-level analgesia, usually postoperatively. Therapy is initiated parenterally (IV/IM); oral ketorolac is only continuation therapy. Multiple boxed warnings cover GI, cardiovascular, renal, bleeding, neuraxial and other risks; total duration of IV/IM plus oral must not exceed 5 days.
indications: Short-term (<=5 days) management of moderately severe acute pain that requires analgesia at the opioid level, usually postoperatively
Oral ketorolac only as continuation of IV/IM therapy

dosage.c: Adult >=65 yr, renal impairment, or <50 kg
dosage.d: IM 30 mg or IV 15 mg single; 15 mg q6h (max 60 mg/day)
20 mg once, then 10 mg every 4-6 hours (max 40 mg/day)

admin: Initiate with IV or IM dosing; oral is continuation only
Give IV bolus over no less than 15 seconds; IM slowly and deeply
Total combined IV/IM and oral duration must not exceed 5 days
Take oral doses with food/milk; use lowest effective dose
moa: Ketorolac non-selectively inhibits cyclo-oxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis. This produces potent analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects; it also inhibits platelet aggregation through reduced thromboxane production.

absolute: Active peptic ulcer disease, recent GI bleeding or perforation
History of peptic ulcer disease or GI bleeding
Advanced renal impairment or risk of renal failure due to volume depletion
As prophylactic analgesic before major surgery; intraoperatively when haemostasis critical
Concomitant aspirin or other NSAIDs; concomitant probenecid or pentoxifylline
Hypersensitivity to ketorolac; history of asthma/urticaria/allergic reaction to aspirin or other NSAIDs (CABG perioperative use)

preg: Avoid NSAIDs, particularly from 30 weeks' gestation, due to risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus and oligohydramnios/renal effects. Ketorolac is contraindicated during labour and delivery because it may adversely affect fetal circulation and inhibit uterine contractions.
lact: Ketorolac is contraindicated in nursing mothers per the label because of potential adverse effects of prostaglandin-inhibiting drugs on the neonate.
renal: Contraindicated in advanced renal impairment and in patients at risk of renal failure from volume depletion. In moderate impairment or patients >=65 yr / <50 kg, reduce the dose (e.g. 15 mg IV q6h, max 60 mg/day) and monitor renal function.
hepatic: Use with caution; reduce dose and monitor for hepatotoxicity. Discontinue if liver disease develops or transaminases rise persistently.

major: Aspirin and other NSAIDs - increased GI bleeding/ulceration (contraindicated together)
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs + diuretics - acute kidney injury ('triple whammy')
minor: May reduce diuretic effect of furosemide
interactions.food: Take with food/milk to reduce GI upset
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - markedly increases GI bleeding risk
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor renal function, CBC, and blood pressure

counsel: Use for no more than 5 days total (injection plus tablets)
Take tablets with food; report black stools, vomiting blood or severe stomach pain
Report reduced urine output, swelling, chest pain or shortness of breath
Do not use if breastfeeding or in late pregnancy
pk: Analgesia begins ~30 minutes after IV/IM dose
Maximum analgesic effect 1-2 hours after dosing
Store at 15-30 C; protect injection from light
pearls: Opioid-level analgesia but with NSAID risks - strictly limited to 5 days total
Oral form is continuation only; never an initial dose
Reduce dose for >=65 yr, <50 kg, or renal impairment
Contraindicated in active/prior peptic ulcer, advanced renal impairment, labour and breastfeeding
Inhibits platelets - avoid around surgery where haemostasis is critical
missed: Ketorolac is used short-term for acute pain. If a scheduled dose is missed, take it when remembered unless near the next dose; do not double up, and do not exceed the daily maximum or 5 days total.
overdose: Overdose may cause abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, GI bleeding, drowsiness, metabolic acidosis and acute renal failure. Management is supportive and symptomatic; activated charcoal may help after recent ingestion; ketorolac is not significantly removed by dialysis.
